prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (policy-only)

- Europe and Brexit
  - A referendum on the final EU deal, including an option to remain.
  - Seek close EU ties: single market/customs union access, reciprocal rights for UK/EU citizens, Erasmus+, policing and security cooperation, and maintenance of EU-derived workers’ and environmental protections.

- Health and social care
  - Immediate 1p Income Tax rise ringfenced for the NHS and social care; explore a dedicated health-and-care tax.
  - Cross-party convention and independent budget watchdog; integrate health and social care.
  - End public-sector pay cap; reinstate nurse bursaries; workforce strategy.
  - Mental health parity with waiting-time standards, crisis care, and local access; support for carers; community/GP access and prevention (e.g., PrEP, obesity and smoking measures, antimicrobial stewardship).

- Education and skills
  - Nearly £7bn extra for schools/colleges; fair funding; protect Pupil Premium; no expansion of selection; local oversight of places.
  - Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium; raise quality.
  - Teachers: lift pay cap; require/expand QTS; funded professional development; cut workload.
  - Curriculum: core entitlement incl PSHE/SRE (inclusive), arts, vocational routes; careers links; mental health in schools; free school meals for all primary.
  - Universities: restore maintenance grants; review finance; widen participation; protect research links; support lifelong learning, apprenticeships, adult learning accounts.

- Economy, tax, business, innovation
  - Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; £100bn infrastructure (housing to 300k/year, fibre-to-premises, rail/roads, schools/hospitals, renewables) via a new Housing & Infrastructure Bank.
  - End public-sector 1% pay cap; protect school funding.
  - Tax: tackle avoidance; review corporate tax base; reverse selected tax cuts; review business rates and consider land value taxation.
  - SMEs: expand British Business Bank; start-up allowance; mentoring; regulatory clarity.
  - Science/tech: protect and expand R&D; hyperfast broadband rollout; digital skills; support creative and green industries.

- Environment, energy, transport, housing
  - Five green laws; insulate 4m homes by 2022; Green Buildings Act (Band C homes by 2035); community energy; Zero‑Waste Act (70% recycling; cut single-use waste).
  - Air quality plan: diesel scrappage; end sales of new diesel cars/small vans by 2025; expand low-emission zones; EV charging network.
  - Energy: net‑zero by 2050; ~60% electricity from renewables by 2030; support storage/CCS/offshore wind/tidal; oppose fracking; conditional role for nuclear; remain in Euratom.
  - Nature/farming/fisheries: Nature Act with legal targets; flood fund; tree planting; animal welfare; reform farm support toward public goods; stronger Groceries Code Adjudicator; sustainable fisheries plan.
  - Housing: 300k homes/year incl 500k affordable; garden cities; lift council/HA borrowing caps; curb land-banking; local powers on second homes; Rent to Own; ban tenant fees, cap deposits; longer tenancies; Help to Rent loans; end rough sleeping via Housing First.
  - Transport: rail franchise reform with public/employee bids; electrification, HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2; rail ombudsman; bus franchising powers; young persons’ bus discount; active travel; no net runway increase; develop regional airports.

- Work, welfare, pensions
  - Promote living wage and pay transparency; gig-economy rights; curb zero-hours abuse; scrap tribunal fees.
  - Uprate working-age benefits with inflation; reform assessments; scrap bedroom tax; align Local Housing Allowance to rents; means-test winter fuel payment for higher-rate taxpayers; retain pension triple lock.

- Rights, justice, policing, security, drugs
  - Retain Human Rights Act/ECHR; digital bill of rights; Leveson 2.
  - Policing: +£300m/year; body cameras; replace PCCs with local boards.
  - Justice: Victims’ Bill; presumption against short sentences; women’s/youth justice reforms; rehabilitation focus.
  - Terrorism: targeted, judicially overseen surveillance; end indiscriminate bulk collection; community-led prevention.
  - Drugs: end imprisonment for possession; legal, regulated cannabis market; shift policy lead to Health.

- Immigration and asylum
  - Efficient system with entry/exit checks; annual skills debate; remove students from migration stats; reinstate post‑study STEM visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL.
  - Safe and legal routes; resettle 50,000 Syrians and 3,000 unaccompanied children; 28‑day detention limit; faster decisions; right to work after six months; protect vulnerable claimants.

- International and defence
  - Support multilateral institutions; maintain 0.7% aid; tighter arms export controls; suspend sales where humanitarian law is breached.
  - Address major conflicts (Syria, Yemen), support a two‑state solution, counter aggression, tackle violent extremism.
  - Defence: spend 2% of GDP; strengthen cyber; minimum nuclear deterrent with three submarines at reduced readiness; improve veterans’ support.

- Democracy and devolution
  - Votes at 16; STV for councils and Westminster; Lords reform; donation caps; stronger lobbying rules; leaders’ debates; modernised campaign finance oversight.
  - Constitutional convention; devolve repatriated powers; further powers for Wales and Northern Ireland; protect common travel area; English devolution on demand; maintain stable inter‑nation funding and address Welsh underfunding.
